rounds.fact: Star ratings lasted until 2010. They were retired because almost everyone rated either 5 stars or 1, so the site switched to thumbs up/down.
Overstock.com built its business selling excess and returned inventory at discount prices, essentially running an online liquidation warehouse.
MSN launched alongside Windows 95 as Microsoft's answer to AOL, bundling a dial-up service with a portal homepage that shipped as the default for millions of new PCs.
Opera was one of the first browsers to introduce tabbed browsing and built-in mouse gestures, features that later became standard across every major browser.
PayPal originally grew by paying users real money just to sign up and refer friends, an aggressive growth tactic that helped it become the dominant way to pay on eBay.
